attributes.description: Alerts when the HTTP 5xx error rate for lambda or edge requests exceeds 2% over a 15-minute window, evaluated separately per log source. This is the primary server-side health signal for a Vercel deployment.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] High HTTP 5xx error rate by log source

investigation_guide.blob:
## High HTTP 5xx Error Rate

### Triage Steps
1. Identify the affected log source (`lambda` or `edge`) from the alert context.
2. Check the Vercel Logs Overview dashboard, filtered to the affected source and `deployment.environment.name: production`.
3. Inspect recent errors: `FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default | WHERE vercel.log.source == "<source>" AND http.response.status_code >= 500 | KEEP @timestamp, http.route, url.path, message, deployment.id, vercel.execution.region | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50`
4. Correlate the error spike with `deployment.id` — did a new deployment ship shortly before the spike started? If so, consider rolling back.
5. Check whether errors are concentrated in a single `vercel.execution.region` (see the regional error skew rule) — this would point to a regional infra issue rather than a code defect.

### Note
`http.response.status_code == -1` (function crash, no response returned) is excluded from this rate — see the dedicated lambda/edge crash-rate rule for that signal.

### Escalation
If the 5xx rate remains elevated after a rollback or hotfix, escalate to the on-call engineer.
